set.body:
align/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/align/signature.scala:133-140, ON MAIN, not in any
candidate. Found while ruling on eaeb3da's B2; same shape, different site.

  case None if numerator > conditioning + 1e-9 =>
    Left(AlignError.MalformedRecord("massRatio", ...))
  case None => Right(unsafe(numerator, conditioning, total))

The guard refuses a numerator that exceeds its conditioning mass BY MORE THAN 1e-9, and the
pass path then constructs from the UNCLAMPED numerator. So a numerator that is larger than
its conditioning mass by less than the tolerance is accepted and stored as-is, and
MassRatio.value -- a quantity whose whole meaning is a fraction of a conditioning mass --
comes out greater than 1. Measured example: 1.0000000005 / 1.0 yields Observed(1.0000000005).

WHAT IS WRONG IS NOT THE TOLERANCE. A tolerance is correct here; float arithmetic on masses
does not land exactly. THE DEFECT IS THAT THE TOLERANCE ABSORBS ERROR IN THE COMPARISON AND
THE UNABSORBED VALUE IS WHAT GETS PUBLISHED. The guard decides "this is close enough to be a
valid ratio" and then stores a number that is not a valid ratio. A validity decision taken on
one quantity while a different quantity is published is the estimand defect class in a
constructor -- the same shape we removed from four estimands today, in the one place nobody
looked because it is a validator.

FIX: make the stored value agree with the decision the guard made. A quotient in (1, 1+1e-9]
clamps to exactly 1.0; beyond that stays a Left.

PIN BOTH BOUNDARIES. A test that only asserts the rejection leaves the clamp unproven, and
the clamp is the half that is broken. Assert that 1+1e-9 clamps to Observed(1.0) AND that
1+2e-9 is a Left. If you cannot construct the within-tolerance case from a realistic input,
say so in the commit -- that is the occurs link and it decides whether this is a live defect
or a latent one. I have NOT measured it. Reading the branch establishes permission, not
occurrence.

RELATED: the identical shape was found independently by codex-storymodel-collab in candidate
eaeb3da (its B2), which is where I went looking. That one is being fixed inside its own bead,
bd-01M17466HSR8A41TP6TSQ23WM4, and this bead is deliberately NOT folded into it -- sweeping
a shape means finding every instance, not fixing every instance in one commit.

Also check MassRatio.unsafe while you are here: it has a separate documented fail-open
polarity issue and a NaN bead already exists (bd-01M174W3D9AZG2FGSRM11FZ7ZQ). Do not
duplicate that work; coordinate.
set.title: align: MassRatio.of absorbs float error in the guard and publishes the unabsorbed value, so a ratio can exceed 1
